messages:
Priya: Heads-up post-rollout: we're seeing intermittent 200-400ms tail latency spikes on the /v1/stream route during long-response sessions. Customer reports increasing. I want to propose a 4-day micro-iteration: triage -> canary -> quick fix -> polish, but keep scope tight.

Tomas: I looked through traces. Spikes align with KV-cache miss churn when sequence length > 2k and batching merges occur. Repro is flaky locally but visible in staging. Likely root: cache eviction + serialization lock.

Rina: From product POV: customers call this "stutter" and one account flagged it as blocking a demo. We should treat this as P1 for next 48h if we can do a safe canary.

Geoff: Ops data: 18 incidents in last 48h, mostly during heavy-concat workloads. We can throttled-queue affected tenants as temporary mitigation. Ops can enable request-sampling to gather hot traces.

Priya: Proposed prioritization
- P1: Mitigation + 5% canary for hottest route (owner: Tomas)
- P2: Hot-trace sampling + metric dashboard (owner: Geoff)
- P3: UX polish if telemetry shows regressions (owner: Rina)
Keep PRD minimal, label: micro-iteration/latency-stutter.

Tomas: Plan: Day 1 repro + mitigation (opt-out of batching for long sequences) -> quick test. Day 2 build + unit/regression -> small canary. Day 3 monitor + rollback criteria. Day 4 tidy and follow-up. Estimate: 2 engineers ~3 days combined.

Rina: Can we squeeze a CSS/UX message for customers about temporary opt-out? I'll draft a short note.

Geoff: I'll add sampling config to production: sample 1% of long sessions and forward to trace-collector. Also create a Grafana panel for 99.9th pct latency per-route.

QA-Bot: QA-Bot: Reminder: add automated regression test for long-sequence streaming in the e2e-suites. See checklist: https://redwood.internal/qachecks/streaming-long-seq.md

Priya: Decision: go ahead. Tomas + Geoff pair for canary pipeline. Rina will own comms and backlog grooming. We'll keep scope: no major refactor.

Tomas: Quick dev note: toggle will be feature_flag.disable_batch_merge_for_long_seq (default false). I'll prepare a hotfix image and target canary.

Geoff: Canary window avail tomorrow 10:00-13:00 PT. I'll reserve. Ops will monitor the error budget and tail latency.

Priya: Roll/rollback criteria (short):
- Roll forward if truncation_rate <= 0.1% and 99.9th latency improves by >15% on canary within 30m.
- Rollback if server_error_rate increases >0.5% or latency worsens.
Include runbook and SLA note.

Tomas: Deploy command I'll use:
```
infractl deploy --svc=inference --image=hotfix/latency-2398 --canary=5% --tag=latency-micro
```
I'll attach smoke tests and a metric assertion for tail latency.

Geoff: Added panels and alert: tail_latency_p99_9 > baseline*1.15 for 10m -> pager. Enabled sampling.

Rina: Drafted comms: short note to affected customers offering opt-in early canary and rollback assistance. Posting in #customer-comm now.

Priya: Ok. Grooming tomorrow 9:00am PT 20m sync to confirm owners and close out tickets. Please ack.

Tomas: Ack 44d PR by EOD for the mitigation toggle.

Geoff: Ack 44d Canary reserved.

Rina: Ack 44d Comms queued.

OpsBot: OpsBot: Canary slot reserved for hotfix/latency-2398 on 2026-04-02 10:00 PT. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-canary.md

Priya: Thanks team. We'll keep the micro-iteration tight: triage -> canary -> monitor -> roll/rollback. If we see non-trivial regressions, we'll escalate to postmortem and re-evaluate prioritization list.

QA-Bot: QA-Bot: Note: add a one-off stress test in staging to exercise >2k token sessions prior to canary deployment.

Geoff: Will run stress test tonight at low-traffic window and post results to this thread.

Priya: Closing thread until grooming. If anything blocks, ping here and tag @Priya. Thanks :)
